steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Guys, I see people ahead! There's army!

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: That way... er, seven? Seven o'clock?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Oh, no worries, we got the message.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: But are you sure that's what you saw? There's not a hint of human life anywhere in these parts... Why would the army be patrollin' out here?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Hand me the binoculars.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: There's very little terrain nearby that would conceal us. Everyone, please hide here for the moment.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: I'll go with you. I'd know the Victorian Army more thorough than you, na?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...Mm. Thank you.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Selmon, come take a look... If I crouch under this rock, the enemy won't see me from any angle, will they?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Hah, not half bad.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Good, then. God, we go through the wastes for four days without a peep, no Catastrophe or savage beasts... and then we hit a roadblock at the very end. Just our luck, you figure.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Now stop sticking your head out, keep low with the rest of us. It's been so long, you still don't trust Reed's lot?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: No, as a matter of fact. It's the bland type like her I least trust.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: She only wants to do stuff that doesn't offend nobody. That way, if she ever makes a mistake, it won't really BE her fault.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: You bloody... You just don't like her stopping us from going to Dublinn.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Maybe. But I don't say nothing to you neither, do I?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...Confirmed. It's a small-scale Victorian deployment, but judging by their equipment, not from a nearby barracks.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Their weapons are highest caliber. If we fought... there's very little chance we'd win.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: They might not be searching for us, but just in case, we'd better hide ourselves. Based on their current advance, they won't catch sight of us.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: You don't give me lip for what I say because nobody listens to what I say.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Anyhow, I'm jealous of how she's taken over my show.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: ...Those troops are coming closer. Budge over, give me a good position to watch 'em.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: *sigh* I'm begging you, don't cause trouble now.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Wh—What's happening? Are they scuffling?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: ...Some group ambushed them at a pass.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: S—So if we'd not stopped to hide just now, we would've been sprung too? Who was waiting there?

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Hey... I can't make out too clearly, but those clothes they're wearing look a bit like Selmon's, don't they?

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: That's gotta be... Dublinn, right?

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: ...Dublinn.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: One dawn eight months ago, just after I'd finished work, I was eating breakfast in a cafe in County Peninsula.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: A voice came from my radio.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: It said, with their flames, they would cleanse Victoria of filth.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: In the name of the Tarans... they would declare war on Victoria.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: They called themselves 'Dublinn'.

steps.name: Special Forces Soldier
steps.text: ...Just a bunch of greedy thugs trying to give themselves a title.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: Thugs?

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: The ones common sense would identify as thugs more or less all died in County Hillock.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: Someone intended on using an entire city of Tarans to test the Taran-born Duke... but didn't anticipate the leader of Dublinn conversely exploiting that.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: After the conclusion of the incident, Dublinn successfully purged all unstable elements from the city, and further gained the surrounding Taran populace's support, escaping intact directly under Victoria's nose.

steps.name: Special Forces Soldier
steps.text: Dublinn's leader is undeniably well-versed in the behavior of nobility.

steps.name: Special Forces Soldier
steps.text: It's no wonder, considering her background and her hidden supporters.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: That leader and her intelligence personnel are both fully aware it was the barracks that shelled the masses with dirty bombs, that being why the truth of the County Hillock incident will never be traced nor pursued.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: However... I've read the reports. All the reports.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: Some say the Dublinn 'Leader' that appeared in County Hillock on that day... is more than one person.

steps.name: Special Forces Soldier
steps.text: That doesn't match up with the other intel we got from the Dukes.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: Have you seen these two jigsaw puzzles?

steps.name: Special Forces Soldier
steps.text: They're exactly the same...

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: As long as the forms are identical, they can fill the same holes. And the moment you put them together like this, most people who cast an eye would treat one piece like the other's shadow.

steps.name: Special Forces Soldier
steps.text: ...Shadow?

steps.name: Special Forces Soldier
steps.text: So that's why you suspect that previous arson case, the one tied to Dublinn...

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: It was only a suspicion at first.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: It was, until... the reaction from that Harmonie Feline fed me some interesting information.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: Who knew the Duke of Wellington would actually turn a blind eye to King Gaeil's other descendant walking freely in the wilds?

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: Madam, as you predicted, someone took the people from those farming households in for questioning this morning.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: I looked into it. They weren't wearing barracks uniform. it seems they're not part of the nearby patrol at all.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Hm... say, if I asked for a holiday and went out traveling, what would the better location be? Leithanien, or Kazimierz?

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Or maybe I'll run off even farther... just maybe, like my good friend from the school days, I'll take a trip to Yan?

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: ...I don't understand what you mean.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: *sigh*.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Forget it. We'll be caught in a snare if we don't tiptoe... but either way, we do need to remedy this as best we can. Ensuring her safety is priority number one.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: You mean...

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: My dear friend, Loughshinny.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: You're sure she's the one they're looking for?

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Well, can you be sure she's not?

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: We've got no other choice. Who let her be 'The Leader' too? We can't allow her to fall into anyone else's hands... especially not the Duke of Caster's.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Come, now. We need to pay 'The Brigadier' a visit.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Selmon, what do we do? You said you'd take us to shelter with a Dublinn squad, and now they're right here in front of us, fighting with Vic's army.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: My gut says we should head in and help the Tarans' troops. My brain says we need to show some loyalty before we join them... I mean, right, right?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: No, no, what are you people on about?! We'd never beat those servicemen!

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: A—And besides... what would Reed's lot think?

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: They're hiding over there. They're not that near us. Maybe they won't see what we're doing.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Oh, God, down goes another...

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: ...We can't just sit here watching Tarans get beat to death, can we?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: ...Fionn, take a look behind. How are Reed's bunch reacting to this?

steps.name: Special Forces Captain
steps.text: All men, pull back! Prioritize shaking pursuit!

steps.name: Special Forces Captain
steps.text: Our investigatory mission is complete! We can't waste our time here. Dublinn's deployed far too many diversions.

steps.name: Special Forces Soldier
steps.text: Captain, human activity at three o'clock.

steps.name: Special Forces Captain
steps.text: ...Who are they?

steps.name: Special Forces Soldier
steps.text: Seemingly normal refugees, with improvised weapons.

steps.name: Special Forces Captain
steps.text: Initiate contact, confirm the true situation. All men, prepare to fight on two fronts.

steps.name: Special Forces Captain
steps.text: Beware the possibility of Dublinn's regular forces disguising as civilians.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Hey, what's he doin' pokin' his head out from the bunker?!

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Oh, the unit noticed him. They're comin' over.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: I'll try and see about negotiatin' with them. I'll tell them it's all civilians here.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: No. Tara's local barracks—would never trust civilians...

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...They've never protected us before.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Hah... hah... hi—hi there... we're Tarans, we want to join Dublinn...

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: ...Hello?

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Guh—wh—what the hell?!

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Fall back!

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: ...Retreat ASAP. These two units are attacking us simultaneously.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: But aren't Dublinn... meant to be defending Tarans?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: ...I can't give you a response. All I know is these soldiers are already dead.

steps.name: Special Forces Captain
steps.text: Standard piledriver spear, Vouivre... you're ex-Tempest Platoon personnel, aren't you?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Oh! Have we met before?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Well, since we're not strangers, that makes things easier. We're not an ambush, and we've got nothin' to do with Dublinn either. You've gotten the wrong idea about us.

steps.name: Special Forces Captain
steps.text: ...Hah, surprise, surprise. That Fischer boy only sent me out here to follow a trail, and here we've run into his true goal headfirst.

steps.name: Special Forces Captain
steps.text: No, I'd wager he sent me here specifically to wait until you ran into us.

steps.name: Special Forces Captain
steps.text: Bagpipe, why are you protecting the Tarans?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Eh? Because that's our duty, right? The Tarans are Victorians too.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: If we've cleared up the misunderstandin', are we able to ceasefire? Attackin' civilians is a violation of military discipline.

steps.name: Special Forces Captain
steps.text: ...What gives you the continued right to say that?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Eh? What's wrong with me?

steps.name: Special Forces Captain
steps.text: You seem to not be duly aware of the situation here.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Oh, excuse me, I'm very well aware.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: My friend said you wouldn't protect Taran civilians, and I've just confirmed she was right.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: You're the same as that old Colonel Hamilton back in County Hillock, na?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: So even though I'm discharged? I'm positive now, I still have to fulfil a Victorian serviceman's duty, and do what you're not willin' to do—

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Defend these civilians' lives.

steps.name: Special Forces Captain
steps.text: Then let me ask. Have you ever inquired into that white-haired Vouivre's identity?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: C—Come on, let's go, Selmon...

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Everyone's looking to escape!

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Ugh, now's not the time to be stubborn!

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: I know this is hard to take, but... what Ch'en said seems true... so, let's get away for now?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Come on, survive first, then we can talk after...

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: ...Who's that you're staring at? Wait, it can't be...

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: ...Bro.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: There, Fionn... Your wound is like last time's. It's not too severe.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: But—it'll still hurt.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Nrgh, that's whatever... as long as I don't see blood. Anything else flies with me.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Coward. You said you'd help Selmon. All you've done was scarper with her on your shoulders.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: N—Nothing wrong with that, at least we made it out. All of us made it out.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: ...*sigh*.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Reed, I need to ask something... I've been wanting to ask it all day.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: You and your friends seem to be professionals with this stuff. But—I still just don't get. Why do you say those people... those Dublinn people are dead?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Is there any off-chance they're sleepwalking? Maybe it's that witchcraft from the legends that makes people lose their consciousness?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Just... just on the off-chance, that they are sleepwalking, we could go and wake them up...

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...We can't. I wish I could provide you some consolation, but—it's a unique Originium Arts I recognize.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: *sigh* Alright. I'm just a little frightened myself. What's Selmon gonna think, though?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: What's... wrong with her?

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Oh, go on and tell, Fionn, we all know her. You were the one vouching for her since the beginning. She's a good girl. We wouldn't have come with her otherwise.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: The... the truth is, I actually know her because she robbed me, once.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: We sat down and got talking with one another in the end, of course. She just wanted a pair of sturdy boots. Her brother was out in the snow that winter with half his soles worn through, feet frostbitten something hideous.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: So you gave her yours?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: No, actually. Her brother went off to Dublinn. I was only in time to cover for them. Couldn't do them any solid boots quickly enough.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Fact is, she's been out here this whole time looking for her brother.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: What? She brought us to join Dublinn just for that?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: No, it's more than that, it's...

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: She wanted to join Dublinn along with her brother, she just ran away on the way there. That was two years ago.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: ...Think how tough it must've been on her, catching up to her brother today.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: ...Say, how do you think my family's doing?

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: They're still back living in the village. It's about time they replaced the roofing straw. Once we find a place to stop over, I'm getting a Messenger to ask how they're doing.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: It's alright, I'm sure they're fine. I'll help you find that Messenger, come then.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Grand.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: ...But where are we going? We chased a Dublinn squad that was all dead people, and Selmon's not found her own. Where should we head now?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: *sigh* Reed, what do you...

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: ...Reed? Where'd she go?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: ...Thirteen, fourteen, fifteen... three less than in the day.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: ...I just don't get it. What kind of Originium Arts is this? Makes me sick looking at it.
She squats behind a boulder, looking around.
The soldiers keep marching for their heart's destination, upon the twilight wilds.
The colors of the Dublinn uniform fade beneath layers of mud and soil. They seem as if held in a silhouette, one lit by a glimmer from somewhere unknown.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: I just need to... pounce, then retreat, and I'll be fine.
A hundred meters.
They turn to walk straight for the boulder Selmon hides behind.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Tch, he's at the back of the squad. Looks like he didn't get to be the leader. Made himself out so bloody big in all his letters.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: They're headed for... yeah, same direction as the letters said.
Fifty meters.
Selmon clenches the wooden cudgel in her fist.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: ...Is the city you're heading for that important to you?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Who's telling you to head on? You'd still go, even if you died?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Even though you're being battered by—wind, and rain, and all these people one after another? You'd still go?
Thirty meters.
She remembers the first time she saw Dublinn's troops, two years ago.
They told her, once she was decided, she could come to them. The Leader would give all Tarans a place to survive.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: ...I'm sorry.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: I... never could be as sure as you were. You never looked back, but I did.
She rushes out.
Like those Victorian soldiers in the daytime did, like Ch'en did, these people that have ceased to be can be knocked down again, so long as every attack comes swiftly enough, ferociously enough.
Until they'll sleep peacefully in the soil of Tara, never called to stand again.
The soldier does not fall.
He merely stumbles for a moment from the blow to the neck, and then swiftly spins around, pulling out his sword.
He is ghastly silent.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: You lot! Out of my way! I'll send you all right back with him!

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: No, I will, I'll do it!

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: I was just here to find my brother, but you're all the same...

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: (Silently attacks)

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: —Piss right off! At least say something!

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Grgh...

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Square, that was...

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Hah, bloody hell. Head, chest, it's just not enough, is it.
Her cudgel flies out of her hand blocking the next attack.
And in that moment, the soldier's mask falls off.
She feels a sort of illusion for a moment. As if the way he brandishes his weapon slows, for a fraction of an instant.
As if her brother is about to give him both his hands, like when Victoria's police accosted them in younger times, shielding her in his embrace.
And then she sees his familiar face all so clearly.
His forehead drips no blood, and his eyes turn no look to his little sister.
Those eyes gaze to the distant, vague horizon, a rage of firelight longing, burning within.
—Just like the night he decided he'd seek out Dublinn.
And Dublinn soldiers surround them. Selmon blankly, dazedly, reaches a hand out to the man before her.
Admiration, aspiration, guilt. Regret.
All swallowed up by the ice-cold fire that her fingertips brush.
Fear.
All she is left with is fear. The fear of that longing, maniacal, burning unto death.
And before time can move again, flames blaze high, incandescent sparks blossoming into the night sky.
So close her fingers could almost touch, a flame blooms forth, and vanishes again before she can grasp it. The soldier falls over, to the ground, and never makes another whisper.
